'''Nathalie Drach-Temam''' (born 1966) is a French computer scientist who became the President of [[Sorbonne University]] in 2021 and was re-elected in 2025. She was the first woman to hold that role in almost a thousand years of the university's history. She championed the idea of adding women's [[List of names on the Eiffel Tower|names to the Eiffel Tower]] after it was suggested by a Sorbonne student.

==Biography ==
Drach-Temam was born in 1966 in [[France]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=La biographie de Nathalie Drach-Temam, Présidente de Sorbonne Université |url=https://www.letudiant.fr/educpros/personnalites/drach-temam-nathalie.html |access-date=18 June 2026 |website=L'Étudiant.fr |archive-date=4 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250804231600/https://www.letudiant.fr/educpros/personnalites/drach-temam-nathalie.html |url-status=live }}</ref> She studied mathematics<ref name="mathsboss" /> and received her PhD in computer science from the [[University of Rennes]] in 1994 with a dissertation on [[pipeline (computing)|pipeline]] optimization in microprocessors. Her doctoral adviser was [[André Seznec]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Drach-Temam |first=Nathalie |title=Optimisation du pipeline sur les processeurs monocomposants |date=1 January 1994 |degree=These de doctorat |publisher=Rennes 1 |url=https://theses.fr/1994REN10106 |archive-date=9 June 2026 |access-date=17 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260609090048/https://theses.fr/1994REN10106 }}</ref>

After holding teaching and research positions at the [[University of Rennes]] in, the [[Paris-Sud University|University of Paris-Sud]] and [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation|INRIA]], the French institute for computer science and automation, Drach-Temam became a professor in 2004, first at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (UPMC) and later at [[Sorbonne University]]<ref name="thepie">{{Cite web |title=Nathalie Drach-Temam |url=https://thepienews.com/movers/nathalie-drach-temam/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=The PIE News |language=en-GB}}</ref> after UPMC merged with it. She specialized in designing computer processors.<ref name="thepie" /> 

Drach-Temam was a Professor of mathematics and computer science<ref name=lstar/> and was elected President of Sorbonne University in 2021.<ref name="thepie" /> She was the first woman to hold that role in almost a thousand years of the university's history.<ref name=lstar/> In her new role she made a point of not avoiding controversial subjects like [[Brexit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 March 2022 |title=Universities must not shirk public role, says Sorbonne president |url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/universities-must-not-shirk-public-role-says-sorbonne-president |access-date=21 June 2026 |website=Times Higher Education |language=en |archive-date=18 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250518095931/https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/universities-must-not-shirk-public-role-says-sorbonne-president |url-status=live }}</ref> She completed her first term in 2025.<ref name="term2" /> During that term, she received a proposal from Bernaud Rigaud, a Sorbonne student who chaired a group tasked with generating new ideas. Rigaud, who also worked as a tour guide at the [[Eiffel Tower]], noted that the 72 names commemorated on the tower were all male and suggested that women should be added to the memorial.<ref name="hypat" /> The university, together with Drach-Temam, agreed to support the initiative.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z-8vNEEoE6U |title=Découvrez le projet Hypatie pour la Tour Eiffel |date=11 February 2023 |last=Défis Sorbonne |access-date=17 June 2026 |via=YouTube |archive-date=18 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260618030143/https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop&v=Z-8vNEEoE6U |url-status=live }}</ref> The proposal was later taken up by the [[Mayor of Paris]], and [[Femmes et Sciences]] was tasked with selecting the 72 women to be honoured.<ref name="hypat">{{Cite web |title=The Hypatia project: engraving the names of 72 women scientists on the Eiffel Tower |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en |archive-date=16 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260616203243/https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/hypatia-project-engraving-names-72-women-scientists-eiffel-tower |url-status=live }}</ref>

In June 2025, ahead of the election for her second term, Drach-Temam announced that the Sorbonne University would be restructured. This was not well received in affected areas of the university.<ref name="term2">{{Cite news |date=17 June 2025 |title=A Sorbonne Université, crise ouverte entre la présidente et deux doyennes de faculté |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/campus/article/2025/06/17/a-sorbonne-universite-crise-ouverte-entre-la-presidente-et-deux-doyennes-de-faculte_6613796_4401467.html |access-date=17 June 2026 |work=Le Monde |language=fr |archive-date=25 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250725223855/https://www.lemonde.fr/campus/article/2025/06/17/a-sorbonne-universite-crise-ouverte-entre-la-presidente-et-deux-doyennes-de-faculte_6613796_4401467.html |url-status=live }}</ref> However, later in 2025, she was re-elected for another four-year term.<ref name="mathsboss">{{Cite web |title=Nathalie Drach-Temam |url=https://franceuniversites.fr/membre/nathalie-drach-temam/ |access-date=17 June 2026 |website=[[France Universités]] |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

She announced in October 2025 that Sorbonne University would no longer participate in the ''[[Times Higher Education World University Rankings|Times Higher Education rankings]]''. The [[University of Zurich]] had already made a similar move and Yale, Harvard and Columbia universities had abandoned a similar set of rankings. Drach-Temam criticised the rankings because the methodologies were not transparent and they could not be reproduced or questioned. She called them "black boxes" and noted they were run by commercial companies.<ref name="norank">{{Cite web |title=Why Sorbonne pulled out of university ranking |url=https://sciencebusiness.net/news/universities/why-sorbonne-pulled-out-university-ranking |access-date=20 June 2026 |website=Science{{!}}Business |language=en |archive-date=20 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260620141146/https://sciencebusiness.net/news/universities/why-sorbonne-pulled-out-university-ranking |url-status=live }}</ref>

In June 2026 she went to [[Benin]] to strengthen Sorbonne's partnership with the {{ill|Sèmè City|fr}} Institute of Technology and Innovation.<ref name=seme/> Seme City is based in Benin's large city [[Cotonou]] and its ambition is to be a world class educational establishment.<ref name="cnn">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.cnn.com/videos/business/2024/04/17/benin-innovation-pkg-04135pseg1-cnni-business.cnn |title=Inside Benin’s innovation hub |date=17 April 2024 |language=en |access-date=25 June 2026 |via=edition.cnn.com}}</ref> The relationship with Sorbonne began in 2017 before she was President. The renewed 2026 agreement was for five years and it will allow exchange of staff, students and ideas between the two bodies.<ref name="seme">{{Cite web |title=A new chapter for the partnership between Sorbonne University and Sèmè City |url=https://www.sorbonne-universite.fr/en/news/new-chapter-partnership-between-sorbonne-university-and-seme-city |access-date=24 June 2026 |website=Sorbonne Université |language=en}}</ref>

==Honours==
In 2015, Drach-Temam was appointed a [[Knight of the Legion of Honour]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=3 April 2015 |title=Décret du 3 avril 2015 portant promotion et nomination |trans-title=Decree of April 3, 2015 concerning promotion and appointment |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFARTI000030440153 |journal=[[Journal officiel de la République française]] |volume=81 |archive-date=24 May 2022 |access-date=17 June 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524093106/https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFARTI000030440153 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, she was awarded the [[Star of Lithuanian Diplomacy]] for improving relations between Lithuania and France.<ref name="lstar">{{Cite web |title=Lithuania’s Diplomacy Star awarded to Nathalie Sylvie Drach-Temam, President of Sorbonne University |url=https://www.urm.lt/en/news/928/lithuanias-diplomacy-star-awarded-to-nathalie-sylvie-drach-temam-president-of-sorbonne-university:44398 |access-date=21 June 2026 |website=Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Lithuania |language=en}}</ref>
